analysis:
The only change in this PR is in the test helper provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Helpers/MockCoordinator.swift, in dropActiveWebSocket (head lines 445-456). It now takes a configurable closeCode (default 1001) and reason (default "mock dropping"), and calls outbound.close(.init(codeNumber: Int(closeCode)), reason: reason). Defaults keep the previous behavior (.goingAway = 1001, same reason string), so existing tests are unaffected. The purpose is to let tests simulate an edge-initiated 1012 close on a Conductor change.

Security review: this is test-only code. It binds to 127.0.0.1:0, is not shipped in the provider binary, and does not touch production trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-011, TB-012), key material, attestation, or authorization. The mock does not validate signatures, by its own documentation, so it adds no production attack surface. The UInt16-to-Int conversion cannot overflow, and an arbitrary close code only affects the local test WebSocket.

The mock's retired telemetry trap (lines 628-650) and the capture structures are unchanged and out of scope for the threat model. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated.

Remaining integration question: the production provider reconnect logic that handles close code 1012 is not in the supplied evidence. Its correctness (for example, not skipping re-attestation or App Attest resume on reconnect, per T-053) should be reviewed in whichever file implements it, not in this test helper.
